Header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Carter (Redwood), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor, Priya Shah, Marco Ruiz (Hightide Finance)

Summary auto-gen: medium quality transcript, some words misrecognized.

00:00 Jesse: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'm jesse carter from redwood inference, i'm the AE on this account, with maya our solutions engineer and tom from success. can you all quick intro?
00:08 Liam: hey liam o'connor, head of ml at hightide. we run a couple of real time risk scoring and a customer chat assistant.
00:14 Priya: priya shah, infra lead, i care about p95 and autoscaling costs and VPC connectivity.
00:18 Marco: marco ruiz, cto, we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private cause of latency and compliance.
00:25 Jesse: great, our goal today is to understand your p95 targets, concurrency, token/sec expectations and whether streaming is required. we'll map those to hosted dedicated and private options and propose a POC.

02:10 Maya: quick question - can you describe typical prompt sizes and workloads? that really changes how batching and kv cache behave.
02:18 Liam: sure - for risk scoring it's short prompts, 30 to 80 tokens, high qps during market hours. p95 needs to be <200ms for the short ones. for chat assistant it's streaming, longer outputs, average 512 tokens but often we stream token-by-token to UI. concurrency for chat peaks around 300 active users, risk scoring peaks at 1500 concurrent small requests.
02:45 Priya: also, we have strict data residency and SOC 2 requirements, so private deployment or dedicated with VPC peering is on the table.

05:00 Jesse: ok good. on the latency numbers - p95 <200ms for 30-80 tokens at 1500 concurrent for risk scoring is quite aggressive but we've seen it before with dedicated pools and optimized kernels. hosted can hit that for smaller concurrency but you'll see cost and variability at scale.
05:24 Maya: to add, p95 is sensitive to batching strategy and sequence length distribution. continuous batching helps throughput but can add tail latency at low qps. our runtime does prefix caching (kv cache) and we can set batching windows to balance qps vs latency.

08:15 Marco: when you say dedicated pools, do you mean reserved GPUs with predictable throughput? what are the autoscale bursts?
08:23 Jesse: yes dedicated = reserved GPU capacity. autoscale policy supports warm pools and burst capacity, you can configure SLO-based routing and fallback to hosted lower tier if capacity is exhausted.

10:02 Liam: streaming - how does streaming affect tokens/sec and p95, especially with many open streams?
10:10 Maya: streaming increases connection overhead and can increase p95 if the model is generating slowly. but our runtime streams as tokens are produced; the key metric is tokens/sec generation and how many concurrently active token streams you can sustain per GPU. for example on a T4-like gpu variant we might see 120-200 tokens/sec per stream at typical sizes, but on A100 or H100 variants you get higher tokens/sec and better p95 performance.

12:40 Priya: can you share concrete benchmark numbers we can use for planning? we need token/sec and p95 for 32/64/512 token outputs across 100/500/1500 concurrency.
12:50 Jesse: yes we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet; for planning numbers only, not guaranteed as they depend on model family, quantization, and sequence length. sample ballpark: dedicated H100-like: p95 ~40-80ms at 64 tokens with 100 concurrency; at 1500 concurrency you'd shard across many workers and keep p95 ~120-250ms depending on model. hosted can do 100 concurrency at p95 ~80-150ms for small prompts.

16:00 Marco: are you supporting quantized models and perf-sensitive kernels? we use a 7b family mostly.
16:09 Maya: yes we support INT8/4 quantization profiles; the runtime chooses kernels and compilation paths automatically. for 7b quantized variants you can see 2-4x improvement in tokens/sec, but there is a small quality delta to validate.

19:30 Liam: what about warmup and KV cache warmup - it matters for p95 for repeated session based requests.
19:38 Maya: we do prefix caching and also application-level cache. for chat sessions the KV cache is sticky per session so repeated turns are much faster (lower p95). for cold starts there is a startup penalty which we measure separately.

22:00 Priya: security - we need SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs, SSO. can you deliver private control plane with customer managed key?
22:10 Jesse: yes, private deployment supports customer KMS/HSM and our enterprise package includes audit logs and SAML/SSO. we'll attach SOC2 report and network diagram.

25:05 Marco: cost tradeoffs - how do we think about cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated?
25:12 Jesse: generally hosted is variable and easier to start; dedicated is committed monthly and gives lower unit cost. we'll include a cost model in the spreadsheet with tokens/sec assumptions. also Redwood Optimize suggests batching/quantization settings to reduce unit cost.

29:40 Liam: for the POC we want to run a token/sec and p95 benchmark with our prompt set. can you run a POC where redwood executes our prompts under 3 concurrency profiles and shares p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec?
29:55 Maya: yes that's the standard POC. ideally you provide prompt set and expected seq lengths; we run dedicated and hosted comparatives. we'll also capture streaming latency (time-to-first-byte and token latency).

33:10 Priya: what telemetry will we get? we need per-request traces, token-level timing, and per-route cost.
33:20 Tom: console exposes per-token cost, latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, traces and exportable logs. we also support pushing traces to your observability cluster via connectors.

36:00 Marco: are there any gotchas around network egress for private deployments?
36:08 Jesse: private deployments can be fully air-gapped; for VPC options we do VPC peering or private link. egress patterns depend on your config; we'll share network diagrams.

40:00 Liam: okay, i'd like to call out our success criteria: p95 <200ms for short prompts at peak concurrency for risk scoring; for chat streaming we need low time-to-first-byte (<120ms) and sustained tokens/sec to keep token-latency small.
40:18 Jesse: noted. so success criteria: (1) risk p95 <200ms at 1500 concurrent 30-80 token requests; (2) chat TTFB <120ms and sustainable tokens/sec to handle 300 concurrent streams with 512-token outputs within your latency budget. we'll run benchmarks to validate.

45:30 Priya: timeline - we want a POC within two weeks, run for 5 business days, then review.
45:38 Maya: we can start next week, we'll need prompt sets, concurrency profiles, and your acceptance tests.

50:00 Jesse: recap of next steps: i'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and POC runbook; maya will prepare POC config; priya will share concurrency distribution and sample prompts; we'll also share SOC2 and network docs.
50:20 Liam: sounds good. also please include a column for model variant and quantization flag in the spreadsheet.

55:00 Jesse: any other questions?
55:05 Marco: none from me. thanks.
55:10 Liam: no, thanks everyone.
55:15 Jesse: great we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.
